Apologises, please provide your feedback here instead. 

Kindly post your discussions in the thread below.

https://discord.com/channels/1131791637933199470/1543760297637187614

Keep this thread purely for feedback only.
D-tide Feedback (New)
- New players can’t feasibly clear Normal mode in the time that it took them to clear a1-a2 on the previous D-Zone
- The jump from Normal mode to Hard mode is WAY too much. A tenfold increase in HP is too high of a gap for players to reasonably clear.
- Locking levelling rewards behind content you can not clear is completely dissuading mid-level accounts that desperately need these to even start playing this D-Zone
- High spenders can barely clear nightmare/madness mode, which dissuades them from even playing.
- As seen from multiple clears it takes around 50-60 turns to clear some content, while no content before this came even CLOSE to this amount of timesink.
- Helot: Catena as a boss is way too over-tuned. The high amounts of HP and punishing playing cards in a card game makes this boss really frustrating, and a slog to get through.

- There is no reasonable middle ground to the new difficulty changes. We went from an a1/a2 equivalent at normal mode to a5/a6 equivalent on hard mode. The people playing a3/a4 are pushed into playing the normal difficulty which is just removing rewards for these accounts for no apparent reason.

- People who normally did a3/a4 as their max clear have no home anymore. They are shoved into the lowest difficulty which makes it that progression is slowed for these players to get to the higher alerts.

- A lot of limited units at high investment can not clear this D-Zone. Not every unit can be as good as each other, this is normal, but having completely maxed out units and not being able to clear dissuades everyone from playing because their favourite character can’t clear anymore in a reasonably high alert.

- The ECOG/Gnosis has proven not to be a good balancing tool with the massive increase in HP. Players feel bad using the Gnosis where they previously couldn’t use them, because it feels like a cheap trick. People generally liked having to crack their brains to make teams that were robust enough to actually clear a4/a5 without dying.
react to the posts if you agree or disagree, thanks for your input

Proposed changes to Ghelot boss:

Only gain fervor on the turns shes using the chain intention and reduce chain damage to match her gameplay identity of chain 3 times into flail

Instead of completely immune to damage,  make her gain 70% fortify instead in phase 2 when shes using flail

Many of the carries in this game are incapable of reaching the damage requirement to clear madness, even at +12 lvl 90, when the game itself was pushed as 'everything can work if you do it right', that's an issue. You need to either lower the hp of the difficulty, or give every awakener a scaling component that makes it possible to stall until they can kill.

About Gnosis use

Using Gnosis in D-Zone was a good idea in principle, but the difficulty shouldn’t be balanced around the assumption that players will use Gnosis.

Gnosis should’ve been a way to help lower-investment players get the rewards they otherwise might struggle to obtain. But right now, the difficulty is simply too high. For many players, there’s basically no hope of clearing the stage in the first place, and using Gnosis once or twice doesn’t even come close to being enough to actually clear it and get the rewards.

And for whales, they generally don’t want to use Gnosis in the first place. They’ve already invested heavily into their characters, so when they find out that they still can’t clear the content without using Gnosis, it’s frustrating in a completely different way. It makes them feel like all the money and effort they put into building their accounts was basically wasted.

Gnosis should be an optional helping hand, not something the difficulty is balanced around.

My feedback on the three biggest issues I have with the new DTide changes. 

I also want to say that I genuinely love this game to death, and wish only the best for it. As much as the recent nerfs and changes concern me, I still hope that the game will change for the better. In other words please please please don’t die on meeeeeee I can’t live without you anymore <:Horla_cry:1357186646294138890>
Couldn't have said it better myself

1. Another thing that really worries me is the environment-specific design for new characters and new D-zone. This feels a lot like the old-school mobile game design where every new event came with a “must-pull event character” who got massively boosted specifically for that event.

That’s basically what this environmental system feels like. What happens next — a Desert environment for the next character? And then that character gets a huge performance boost in the Desert, while being mediocre outside of it?

I really don’t think this is a healthy direction for the game. It creates a situation where characters aren’t necessarily strong because of their actual kit — they’re strong because the current content was designed specifically around them. And once the environment changes, the character can immediately lose a huge part of their value.

2. And regarding character power and D-zone difficulty.
This is a gacha game. A +12 limited character requires a pretty good amount of money and investment. At the very least, players who have invested that much into a limited character should be able to comfortably get all the rewards from the content.

But that’s not what’s happening right now. Because of how insanely fast the difficulty is power-creeping, more and more +12 limited characters are gradually being pushed out of viable teams — Doresain, Helot Catena, Pollux, Daffodil,and many others.

If even fully invested +12 limited characters are constantly being pushed out by new difficulty, how are players supposed to feel comfortable investing in characters?

You can’t keep asking players to spend a significant amount of money on characters while simultaneously making those investments feel obsolete more and more quickly. That’s simply not a healthy long-term direction for a gacha game.

## Poison/Counter cap. ##

Max poison stack is around 200K-400K depending on your team's HP.
Boss has 45000K HP on madness, 14000K on nightmare.
Which is 150 times more and 47 times more HP than max poison stack, this number is simply rediculous.
Poison team will need unreasonable time to kill a boss...even with Xu and Doll's percentage damage.

same thing goes to Counter team as well.
Counter team already struggles in old D-tide contents, they don't have percentage damages, and enemies hit harder and harder, you can't survive.
Now they are basically all out of the picture.....mathematically impossible.

So I propose:
1. Reduce D-tide stats inflations.
2. Raise poison/counter coefficients and caps.
3. Make fixed poison/counter enjoy more types of multiplications rather than dmg amp only.

Finally, please inform us who did the test and why does he/she think poison/counter team still holds up? According to: https://discord.com/channels/1131791637933199470/1537340158863482921/1537347499168366632

1. BIAV clearly introduced these changes to force players to spend more, but mark my words: this will have the exact opposite effect. The "Madness" difficulty isn't just impossible for some, it's so drawn out and unfun that even attempting it feels pointless. Since yesterday, I’ve seen more and more players stating they will only pull for one to four copies of a character, whereas previously they would aim for OE/+12. I am one of those people. I have a few favorite units at +12, and it will stay that way. I have zero reason to pull for something that can be rendered useless in just a few updates or "bugfixed" into oblivion. RIP to all Doresain players.

2. It's incredibly hard to recommend a game that tosses out its entire meta with a single update. The units are clearly unbalanced. Most DPS characters simply cannot dish out the damage required to clear even "Nightmare" without relying on revivals.

3. When a game with this much team-building potential gets reduced to "just use GDoll," "use Vortice," and relying on gimmicks, something is fundamentally wrong.

4. When the game keeps bloating the HP bar, units that deal %HP damage will always outclass even the strongest traditional DPS, unless the scaling is insane. It's simply flawed game design.

5. These changes are either a sign of massive power creep coming in the next few months, or a result of awful planning and a lack of testing. It's probably both, and both scenarios look terrible.

6. What's the point of promising players one thing and then doing another? Why claim that poison and counter are still viable when they were already falling behind before these changes? How can anyone feel confident investing in this game when the dev team pulls the same stunts over and over again?

Personally, I'm tired of the apologies and the "we are a small team" excuses. Do better. Your players have a limited amount of patience.
